security_audit.summary: The skill performs expected outbound requests to BrowserAct and reads BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment. Most Markdown backtick and generic secret alerts are scanner noise, but the skill also encourages API-key disclosure to the agent and does not validate the requested result limit.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that ask users to provide the key in chat. Require BROWSERACT_API_KEY through an environment variable or a configured secret manager.
Parse the limit as an integer and enforce a documented maximum before sending the BrowserAct workflow request.
Document that keywords, task metadata, and authenticated requests are sent to BrowserAct before the workflow runs.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Disclosure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The instructions ask the agent to request the BrowserAct API key, and the script says to provide it to the agent or set an environment variable. This can lead users to paste credentials into chat or terminal logs instead of using a protected secret channel.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited lines explicitly guide users toward providing an API key when configuration is missing. The risk is credential exposure, even though the skill also supports environment variables.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Result Limit
semantic_findings.description: The script forwards the requested limit to the BrowserAct workflow without converting it to an integer or enforcing a maximum. A very large or malformed value could cause unexpected service cost, task failure, or abuse of the external workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code accepts the third command-line argument and sends it as the Date_limit value with no local validation. BrowserAct may enforce its own limits, so the finding is medium confidence rather than certain abuse.

content.value_statement: Manual YouTube result collection is slow and inconsistent. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow to return structured search result data.
actual_capabilities: Searches YouTube through a BrowserAct workflow using keywords, result type, and item limit.
Supports Videos, Shorts, Channels, and Playlists result modes.
Polls BrowserAct task status until completion or timeout.
Prints result fields such as title, description, view count, publish time, and URL.
Uses BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment for authentication.
limitations: Requires a valid BrowserAct API key and access to the BrowserAct service.
Sends search keywords and task metadata to BrowserAct.
Does not open individual YouTube result pages.
Does not validate the requested result limit before submitting the workflow.

use_cases.title: Track Topic Demand
use_cases.description: Collect visible YouTube search results for a topic and compare titles, views, and publish times.

use_cases.title: Build Research Lists
use_cases.description: Gather video, channel, or playlist links for a market, product category, or education topic.

use_cases.title: Prototype Search Workflows
use_cases.description: Test keyword-driven YouTube data collection before integrating BrowserAct results into a larger pipeline.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Video Search
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for a small result set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search YouTube videos for "AI productivity" and return 20 results with titles, view counts, publish times, and URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Shorts Discovery
prompt_templates.scenario: Find short-form content around a topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search YouTube Shorts for "home office setup" and return 50 visible results with links and publish times.

prompt_templates.title: Channel Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Search YouTube Channels for "cybersecurity training" and summarize the channel names, descriptions, and URLs returned by the workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Competitive Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: For each keyword in this list, search Videos with a limit of 100 and compare the top result themes, view counts, and publish recency.

output: A list of matching video titles with descriptions, view counts, publish times, and URLs.
A short status log shows when the BrowserAct task starts, runs, and finishes.

output_examples.input: Search Shorts for a product hashtag.
output_examples.output: The response lists Shorts search results, including visible titles, timestamps, and result links when returned by the workflow.

output_examples.input: Find channels about beginner data analysis.
output_examples.output: The response returns channel search entries with names, short descriptions, and URLs for follow-up review.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY through an environment variable before running the skill.
Use specific keywords and reasonable result limits to reduce noise and service cost.
Review BrowserAct status logs before retrying a failed task.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into chat or shared terminal logs.
Do not use sensitive search terms unless external BrowserAct processing is acceptable.
Do not request very large result limits without confirming service limits and cost.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY so the script can authenticate with BrowserAct.

faq.question: Which YouTube result types can it search?
faq.answer: It supports Videos, Shorts, Channels, and Playlists.

faq.question: Does it open each YouTube result page?
faq.answer: No. It extracts fields from the YouTube search results workflow.

faq.question: Where is data sent?
faq.answer: The script sends workflow parameters and authenticated requests to the BrowserAct API.

faq.question: Can it run without BrowserAct?
faq.answer: No. The script depends on BrowserAct workflow endpoints and a valid account key.

faq.question: What should I do if authorization fails?
faq.answer: Check that BROWSERACT_API_KEY is valid and configured in the environment before retrying.
